title: The Lord Ascended into Heaven
description: The Lord Ascended into Heaven in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns from the Greek Office Books (Paisley, 1904), headed “Stichera of The Ascension”.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Common Metre (8.6.8.6), and this page sets them to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The Lord as-cend-ed in-to heaven That He might from a-bove Send down the pro-mised Par-a-clete On mis-sion of His love.

lines: The Lord ascended into heaven
That He might from above
Send down the promised Paraclete
On mission of His love.
And there the Father for His Son
Had decked a glorious throne;
And clouds, His chariots, bore Him up,
That He might claim His own.
O strangest wonder e'er beheld,
Since ages hoar began,
The angels saw the highest place
Given to a Son of Man.
"O all ye angels praise the Lord,"
The Holy Spirit commands,
"Lift up your gates, ye princes high,
Ye nations, clap your hands."
To God the Father throned on high,
And to the Son be praise,
And to the Spirit — Three in One,
From age to age, always.

source: John Brownlie, Hymns from the Greek Office Books (1904)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Greek, public domain, as printed in Hymns from the Greek Office Books; set to YORK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
